display: Marine biologist at a coastal research institute in Lisbon, developing a seaweed-based bioplastic resin. I also run a small Thursday bouldering group.

signals.text: My lab has a promising seaweed resin, but the grant wants a real consumer product prototype by next July and I only have small cast discs and test bars.
I don't know who to build a first product with. Packaging and cutlery are the obvious candidates, but I have no designer or maker to work with.
I'm stuck on casting a 20x20 cm flat panel. My mould leaks and the resin shrinks at the edges.
I just got 500 h of UV weathering results. Our resin yellowed much less than a commercial bio-epoxy control, and I'm not sure whether that is enough to build a product around.
A grant interim report is due on 9 October, and the funder wants to see something concrete, not just characterisation data.
My beach-cast seaweed survey on the Cascais coast has been paused since July because the field assistant left. The data is half unlabelled.
My Thursday bouldering group has grown to about nine people, and I'd like someone with first aid training to come along.
I am tired and I keep overworking. My forearm is injured from climbing and I won't rest it.
I'm fostering an anxious rescue dog. He is meant to be temporary, but I'm getting attached and may end up needing a plan for him.
I'd like to find a way to work at the same place as my long-distance partner in Norway without giving up my research.
I'm quietly worried that my postdoc contract won't be renewed after next July.
I find it uncomfortable to say my material is promising when we don't yet have a product, and I'd like to be able to say so honestly.

offers.text: I know how to make and characterise seaweed-derived bioplastic resins. I have made three documented batches and can explain the process and results.
I can run UV weathering, mechanical tensile testing and vacuum-oven degassing on small samples at my institute, subject to the shared-equipment schedule.
I have contacts at two seaweed farms near Peniche that sell off-spec biomass cheaply, and I can introduce people to them.
I have silicone and 3D-printed moulds for casting discs, bars and tiles, and I can cast small test pieces for a collaborator.
I can estimate how much Rugulopteryx and Sargassum washes ashore on the Cascais coast, and I have a partial monthly dataset.
I can read Norwegian and speak Portuguese, English and Spanish fluently, so I can help with documents, translation and conversations in those languages.
I run a weekly Thursday bouldering session in Lisbon, and I can bring beginners in and get them started.
I can explain seaweed materials and marine biomass clearly to non-specialists, such as designers, makers and funders.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a product designer or small maker studio. We would like to make a small run of tiles, coasters or packaging prototypes from a new bio-based material, and we need a materials partner.
catchers.can: I can supply cast material and test data (UV stability, mechanical properties), and I can iterate on a shape with you toward a prototype that fits the July milestone.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to design or produce a physical object in the 20 cm range, rather than only doing branding or concept work?

catchers.hypo: I work with moulds and casting for resins or ceramics. I've seen shrinkage and edge leaking on large flat panels before, and I might be able to help.
catchers.can: I can share my current mould design and failure pattern so you can advise, and I can test a new mould or casting approach in my lab.
catchers.confirm: Have you solved edge shrinkage or leakage on flat panels of about 20x20 cm, in any water-based or gel-like casting material?

catchers.hypo: We are a company that needs a durable bio-based material for outdoor or sunlit use, and we are looking for something that resists UV yellowing.
catchers.can: I can share my 500 h UV weathering results against a commercial control and discuss whether the material fits your use.
catchers.confirm: Is UV colour stability a real requirement for your product, and are you able to evaluate a small batch of cast samples?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse, paramedic or climbing first-aider in Lisbon, and I'd like to help out at a beginner-friendly climbing session.
catchers.can: My flatmate is a nurse at Santa Maria hospital with shift work and may be able to refer first-aid contacts or step in occasionally. I can also invite you to the Thursday bouldering group.
catchers.confirm: Are you available on Thursday evenings in Lisbon, and do you have current first-aid or emergency-care training?

catchers.hypo: I work on seaweed or aquaculture in Norway, or at a feed or marine biotech company in Bergen, and I'm looking for collaborators in Portugal.
catchers.can: I have a personal connection to someone in the aquaculture sector in Bergen and can make a gentle introduction once there is a concrete fit.
catchers.confirm: Do you have a specific project involving seaweed biomass, rather than a general networking request?

catchers.hypo: I'm a student or volunteer in marine biology and I'd like field experience counting washed-up seaweed on the coast near Lisbon.
catchers.can: I can hand over the Cascais beach-cast survey protocol and shared spreadsheet, and help label the existing data.
catchers.confirm: Can you commit to regular beach visits across several months, and are you comfortable entering data into a shared spreadsheet?

catchers.hypo: I run a company that wants to try out a bio-based material and I'm looking for a research partner who can also help with funding applications.
catchers.can: My supervisor and I can talk about whether a joint project fits our grant timeline, and I can bring the data we already have.
catchers.confirm: Is your timeline compatible with a prototype in hand by about July next year?

catchers.hypo: I'm a dog foster coordinator or a trainer used to anxious rescue dogs, and I'd like to help someone who may adopt one.
catchers.can: I can talk about what has worked with my current foster dog, and I may be able to help find a good long-term home or adopter.
catchers.confirm: Do you have hands-on experience with fear-based or noise-sensitive dogs, rather than general dog training?

forbids.text: I will not use petroleum-based hardeners in any final product.
I avoid working weekends in the lab.
Everything has to fit before the funding ends after next July.
I do not share unpublished formulation details with strangers.
I can only use the institute's shared UV chamber in two-week booking slots.

projects.name: SWR-3 first product prototype
projects.text: Turn the seaweed resin into a physical consumer prototype, for example tiles, packaging or cutlery, by July next year.
roles_needed: industrial partner with a use case

projects.name: Beach-cast biomass survey
projects.text: Monthly counts of Rugulopteryx and Sargassum washing up on the Cascais coast, restarted with a new field assistant and cleaned-up data.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I will share test results, grant deadlines and milestones, and details of my moulds and equipment.
policy.t2: When the fit is clear and I trust the other party, I will talk about my contract worries, my long-distance relationship and how stressed I really am.
policy.never: I will never share unpublished formulation details, my salary, or any details of my partner's family.
